judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Content Standards under Strand 1: Number (same statement-type grain), but in different Sub-Strands: B6.1.1.3 'Demonstrate understanding of factors, multiples and prime numbers from 1 to 100' (Counting, Representation, Cardinality & Ordinality; source context shows HCF/LCM via prime factorisation) and B6.1.2.4 'Demonstrate understanding of division of a 2 or 3-digit number by a 1 or 2-digit number' (Number Operations; indicator context shows dividing 3-digit by 1-digit numbers). There is genuine conceptual coherence — divisibility, factors and multiples underpin and are reinforced by multi-digit division — so the pair is substantively connected. However both sit at the same canonical rank (BASIC 6, rank 2) and the evidence does not substantiate one as developmentally supporting the other (division procedure and factorisation each draw on the other), so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment rather than either buildsTowards direction. producer_judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Content Standards under Strand 1: Number (same statement-type grain), but in different Sub-Strands: B6.1.1.3 'Demonstrate understanding of factors, multiples and prime numbers from 1 to 100' (Counting, Representation, Cardinality & Ordinality; source context shows HCF/LCM via prime factorisation) and B6.1.2.4 'Demonstrate understanding of division of a 2 or 3-digit number by a 1 or 2-digit number' (Number Operations; indicator context shows dividing 3-digit by 1-digit numbers). There is genuine conceptual coherence — divisibility, factors and multiples underpin and are reinforced by multi-digit division — so the pair is substantively connected. However both sit at the same canonical rank (BASIC 6, rank 2) and the evidence does not substantiate one as developmentally supporting the other (division procedure and factorisation each draw on the other), so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment rather than either buildsTowards direction.
